This page opens every instrument of the [Atlas](atlas.qmd) at the single
snapshot its vectors were built from and shows it the way the project reads it,
where the consolidated text is cut into a hierarchy of books, titles, chapters and
articles, and each article into its paragraphs, points and subpoints, and every
node carries a small badge with its type, its identifier and its number. The
aim is to let anyone check that reading by eye, to find the places where it goes
wrong, and to report them from the page itself.

A badge names a node in the vocabulary of Akoma Ntoso, a standard for legal
documents, and hovering over it gives the Mexican term for it. What the vocabulary
calls a paragraph is a *fracción* in a Mexican law, a point is an *inciso*, and a
level is an *apartado*. The *Raw* button of any node shows the exact Markdown that
node was read from, and the *Raw* mode of the whole page shows the document once,
with every excerpt underlined and any character that belongs to no excerpt
marked in red.

The outline on the left follows the same hierarchy. An annex that the Court's
text numbers after a chapter, such as *Annex 2-A* of chapter 2, is shown under
that chapter, and an appendix under the annex or the instrument that it closes,
each one named by its own kind, so that *Annex 2-A* and *Appendix 1* are never
mistaken for each other.

An excerpt is the piece of text that the Atlas compares, which is one article,
one heading, one introduction, one table, one stretch of loose text or the
preamble, each with its own vector. An introduction is the text that a title,
chapter or section opens with before its first article or its first subdivision.
A table is a run of rows that the consolidated text carries outside any article,
and the page draws it as a table; a long one is cut at a row boundary into
several excerpts, each of which has its own address made of the table's
identifier and the number of the part.
Not every excerpt is compared with the rest of the corpus, because a heading
and a transitory article say little about how two instruments relate, so only the
remaining ones, called compared excerpts, carry nearest texts. Opening the
*Nearest texts* of one lists the five closest texts that live in other
instruments, each with its similarity, and a text that several instruments
share appears once with the others named under it. The similarity is the one
given by the Qwen3 Embedding 4B model, the *4B* option of the Atlas, and
following a link opens that other instrument at the excerpt in question.

Seven flags describe what the reading found. A flag is a count and never a
judgement, since many of them are legitimate in a given law, and the table at the
top ranks the instruments by their sum so that the likeliest problems come first.

```{=html}
<ul class="instruments-flag-meanings">
<li><strong>Loose</strong> is text that no rule placed inside an article.</li>
<li><strong>Repeated number</strong> marks two articles that ended up with the same identifier outside the transitory section, that is the same number in the same place of the outline, so that the second could only be kept apart with a suffix. The same number in two different containers, article 1 of Part 1 and of Part 2, is not a repeat.</li>
<li><strong>Number gap</strong> is an article whose number does not follow the previous one in its own container.</li>
<li><strong>Over window</strong> is an excerpt longer than the embedding model's window, whose vector was computed on a truncated text.</li>
<li><strong>No articles</strong> means the instrument has no article at all.</li>
<li><strong>Uncovered</strong> counts the characters of the document that fall in no excerpt, no annotation and no frontmatter.</li>
<li><strong>No transitory section</strong> says only that the instrument has none.</li>
</ul>
```

The documents themselves are not part of the site's source. They are the
`atlas-instruments` release of the repository, which the publishing workflow
downloads and unpacks next to this page, and the page fetches one file only when
an instrument is opened. An address such as `instruments.html?c=leyes&k=ccf#art_1`
opens an instrument and an excerpt directly, and the browser's back button
returns to the previous one.

:::
